observations: A rounded figure leans sharply forward, one arm extended back and one leg lifted, set against a flat yellow-green field divided by a hard black diagonal at the lower third.
The body is built from dense overlapping black lines with flashes of pale blue, yellow, and pink running through the torso, giving the surface a layered, scribbled texture.
The oversized head tilts downward and contains a tight cluster of red star-like marks against a lighter interior, contrasting with the otherwise cool-toned body.
reading: The figure pitches forward at a steep angle, weight committed to a single planted foot while the other leg trails behind. That lean reads as momentum or near-fall rather than stillness. Dense crossed lines fill the body without settling into smooth volume, and the red marks locked inside the head sit apart from everything else — contained but insistent. The flat yellow-green behind it offers no surface to push against.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #54 and nnxyz nnotb #56. All three feature a single figure on a flat ground, but #55 replaces #54's saturated red field and loose white arcs with a split yellow-green and black ground.

connections.reason: Both place a single figure mid-motion on a flat ground using dense overlapping lines, but #54 spreads limbs wide across a red field while #55 compresses the form into a forward lean against a split yellow-green and black ground.
Both share the same yellow-green background and use red marks as a focal accent — in #130 red lines cross the face broadly, while in #55 they concentrate inside the head as a tight cluster.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the black diagonal cut the figure's body, and how does that edge change the way the planted foot reads?
ambiguities: The red marks inside the head could be read as a separate drawn element or as part of the head's surface texture; the image does not resolve which.
Title order and recorded creation order align for this work, but metadata notes gaps and variants exist across the full nnotb family, so broader sequence continuity cannot be assumed.
